title: Stop the guard admitting an unconfigured advisor and missing the two-agent ambiguity
action: REVIEW P2 x2, same file family, both about the guard answering a question wrongly. Read both findings in docs/history/model-role-split/reports/review-r2.md. (1) guard.rs:55-59 inserts every slot_for_kind slot into known_roles UNCONDITIONALLY, advisor included, configured or not. So classify_marker returns Marker::Role for [bee-tier: advisor] on a host with no advisor, the unconfigured-role refusal never fires, and the dispatch falls through Resolved::Budget to allow with no model param — inheriting the session model. That is verbatim the outcome the refusal text at model_guard.rs:152-163 exists to prevent, and bee dispatch prepare --role advisor REFUSES on the same host, so one question has two doors and two answers. (2) model_guard.rs:760 guards the two-agents ambiguity on the literal t == generation. Every freshly onboarded host now configures code, which aliases to generation, so [bee-tier: code] walks past the check and is repaired onto bee-gather — the READ-ONLY agent — and an execution dispatch then dies later at the write guard with the audit line naming the wrong agent. Derive the condition instead of naming it: the ambiguity exists when more than one rendered agent serves the canonical role, so ask that. The test that should have caught it iterates ROLE_AGENTS keys, so no alias spelling is ever exercised — extend it over ROLE_ALIASES spellings too. Run your verify with --no-fail-fast.

truths: A marker naming a role the host does not configure is refused, whatever that role is called — advisor included
The guard and dispatch prepare give the same answer for the same role name on the same host
The two-agent ambiguity is detected by an alias spelling, not only by the table's own key
The ambiguity condition is derived from the agent table rather than naming a role literal
The tests exercise alias spellings, and would fail on the pre-fix code
